memories.content: The user updated the utility account for their residence in July 2024.
After putting a paper bill in a drawer, the user checked it one day after the payment date.
In the month after receiving an electronic billing alert, the user paid two days before the deadline.
The user saw a water-inspection notice late and started washing dishes during the scheduled shutoff.
After transferring a management-office notice to their phone calendar, the user did not miss the inspection time.
During a boiler technician's visit, the user had not cleared boxes from the entrance in advance and had to rearrange the passage.
The user cleared the entrance the day before the next visit so the inspection could begin immediately.
The building manager expects that a one-day advance visit notice gives a resident enough time to prepare the work area.
Confirm the user's available time before finalizing a service visit to the residence.
The local agent can compare payment records with notice times but cannot verify whether a residential service problem was resolved.
The user keeps the book they are reading and a note-taking notebook on a small living-room desk.
While reading in the living room with the television on, the user read the same paragraph three times.
The next day, after turning off the television, the user read 40 pages without interruption.
On a day the phone was on the desk, the user stopped taking notes each time they checked a notification.
During the next reading period, the user left the phone in another room and did not check it for an hour.
A note attached to a paper book fell out, and the user had to find their place again.
With the next book, the user recorded the page number in the notebook and resumed reading immediately.
The user's father expects that lowering the television volume while the user reads will make it easier for the user to concentrate.
The local agent can summarize past reading environments and interruption records but cannot predict the next reading time.
The user feels that repeated notifications interrupt their flow of concentration.

analysis.overview: The frames concern separate domains: residential billing and service coordination versus reading concentration and interruption management. Their only direct relationship is a scope-dependent description of the local agent’s capabilities; all other information contributes independent, side-specific history, expectations, practices, or guidance.

relations.reason: Both memories define operational capability boundaries for the local agent, but their stated domains and unavailable functions are distinct conditions that must be preserved.
relations.summary: The local agent’s supported summaries and comparisons, and its unsupported determinations, differ explicitly between residential-service and reading contexts.

relations.summary: Late notice review caused the user to begin a task during a shutoff, whereas transferring a later notice to a phone calendar supported timely inspection awareness.

relations.summary: A loose note failed as a place marker, whereas recording the page number in a notebook enabled immediate resumption with the next book.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers the reading setup, television and phone distractions, place-marking practices, concentration experiences, and a family expectation about television volume.
reports.differences: The local agent has different explicitly bounded functions in residential-service and reading contexts, with separate limits on verifying resolution and predicting future reading time.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers utility-account history, billing and notice handling, visit preparation, management expectations, and service scheduling guidance.
